title: Tito-Stalin Split Consolidates — Yugoslavia Expelled from Cominform
note: Expulsion from Cominform occurred June 28, 1948; the event year of 1949 represents consolidation period. Minor framing issue — the actual expulsion was 1948, but 1949 as 'consolidation' is defensible.

title: Workers' Self-Management Law Enacted — Yugoslavia Diverges from Soviet Model
note: Basic Law on Management of State Economic Enterprises passed by Yugoslav Federal Assembly on June 26, 1950. Facts confirmed.

title: New Yugoslav Constitutional Law Strengthens Republican Structures
note: 1953 Constitutional Law came into effect January 13, 1953. Note: the label 'Brioni Constitution' is not standard — this name is not used in sources, but the 1953 amendments are real and correctly described. Minor naming inaccuracy only.

title: Belgrade Conference Launches Non-Aligned Movement
note: First NAM conference held September 1-6, 1961 in Belgrade. Tito, Nehru, Nasser confirmed as founding leaders. Correct.

title: New SFRY Constitution Proclaims Socialist Federal Republic
note: Constitution adopted April 7, 1963; renamed state SFRY. Kosovo's status elevated to match Vojvodina as autonomous province. Facts confirmed.

title: Yugoslav Economic Reform Introduces Market Mechanisms
note: 1965 Yugoslav economic reform (decentralization, liberalization, labor emigration) is well-documented. Facts confirmed.

title: Aleksandar Ranković Removed — Serbian Security Apparatus Curtailed
note: Brioni Plenum held July 1, 1966. Rankovic removed after wiretapping scandal. Description says 'bugged Tito's quarters' — confirmed. Facts correct.

title: Student Protests in Belgrade — 'Red University' Uprising
note: Strike began night of June 2, 1968. Students renamed university 'Red University of Karl Marx'. Tito's televised speech on June 9 defused protests. Facts confirmed.

title: Kosovo Albanians Gain Cultural Rights — Albanian-Language Education Expanded
note: Event year 1971 is approximate; University of Pristina was established in 1970, not 1971. Minor year discrepancy — cultural expansion trend in early 1970s confirmed.

title: Yugoslavia's 1974 Constitution Grants Kosovo and Vojvodina Near-Republican Status
note: 1974 constitution gave provinces near-republican powers including de facto veto over Serbian assembly decisions and separate federal representation. Facts confirmed.

title: Tito Dies — Yugoslavia Enters Collective Presidency Era
note: Tito died May 4, 1980 in Ljubljana. He was 87 years old (three days short of his 88th birthday, born May 7, 1892). Event says 'age 87' — confirmed correct.

title: Kosovo Albanian Protests Suppressed — Federal Emergency Declared
note: Protests began March 11, 1981 at Pristina University. State of emergency declared April 2, 1981. 9 killed (7 protesters, 2 police), 226 sentenced. Event says 'deaths and hundreds of arrests' — confirmed broadly correct.

title: SANU Memorandum Published — Blueprint for Serbian Nationalism
note: Memorandum leaked and appeared in Vecernje novosti on September 24, 1986. Facts confirmed.

title: Milošević's Kosovo Polje Speech — Rise of Serbian Nationalist Populism
note: Speech occurred April 24, 1987 (not generically 'April 1987'). Milosevic took over Serbian party leadership at 8th session of Central Committee on September 23-24, 1987. Facts confirmed.

title: Yugoslav Hyperinflation Reaches Crisis Levels
note: Event states 'approximately 250% in 1988'. Annual inflation was building through 1988 and exploded to ~2,700% in 1989. The 250% figure for 1988 is plausible as a transitional estimate; sources confirm inflation crisis was severe in 1988. Minor note: hyperinflation properly exploded in 1989-1994, but 1988 crisis conditions confirmed.

title: Anti-Bureaucratic Revolution — Milošević Topples Provincial Leaderships
note: Anti-bureaucratic revolution ('Yogurt Revolution') 1988-1989. Vojvodina, Kosovo, and Montenegro leaderships toppled and replaced with Milosevic loyalists. Facts confirmed.

title: Milošević Gazimestan Speech — Nationalist Maximalism at Kosovo Battle Commemoration
note: Speech June 28, 1989; crowd estimated at ~1 million (range 500,000 to 2 million). Event says 'estimated one million people' — confirmed. Kosovo autonomy revoked same year confirmed.

title: Kosovo Autonomy Revoked — Province Placed Under Serbian Direct Control
note: Constitutional amendments adopted March 28, 1989. Event says 'March 1989' — confirmed. '22 Kosovo Albanians killed in clashes' confirmed by sources. Facts correct.

title: First Multi-Party Elections in Serbia — Milošević and SPS Win Decisively
note: Elections held December 9, 1990. SPS won 48% of popular vote (not 65% as implied for presidential vote). Milosevic won presidency — his presidential vote percentage was higher (~65%) than SPS parliamentary share (48%). The event blends presidential and parliamentary results; broadly accurate.

title: Yugoslavia Begins to Dissolve — Slovenia and Croatia Declare Independence
note: Slovenia and Croatia declared independence June 25, 1991. Ten-day war in Slovenia confirmed. Facts correct.

title: Federal Republic of Yugoslavia Proclaimed — UN Sanctions Imposed
note: FRY proclaimed April 27, 1992. UN Resolution 757 adopted May 30, 1992 (event says 'May 1992' — confirmed). Facts correct.

title: Bosnian War — Serbia-Backed Bosnian Serb Forces Conduct Ethnic Cleansing
note: Bosnian War began April 1992. Serbia-backed ethnic cleansing campaign confirmed by ICTY findings. ICJ found Serbia failed to prevent genocide (2007 ruling). Facts confirmed.

title: Milošević Imposes Blockade on Bosnian Serbs — Diplomatic Positioning
note: Milosevic blockade on Republika Srpska after Karadzic rejected Vance-Owen plan in May 1993 is historically documented. Facts confirmed.

title: Serbian Hyperinflation Peaks — Currency Destroyed
note: Event says 'second-worst hyperinflation in world history with monthly rates exceeding 300 million percent'. Peak monthly rate was 313 million percent in January 1994. Event attributes peak to late 1993/early 1994 — confirmed. Avramovic stabilization program January 1994 confirmed. Facts correct.

title: Srebrenica Genocide — Serbia-Backed Forces Execute 8,000 Bosniaks
note: July 1995, ~8,000 Bosniak men and boys killed. ICTY and ICJ rulings of genocide confirmed. ICJ 2007 ruling found Serbia failed obligation to prevent. Facts confirmed.

title: Dayton Accords Signed — Milošević Trades Bosnian Serb Interests for Sanctions Relief
note: Initialed November 21, 1995 in Dayton, Ohio (not 'Ohio' generically — Wright-Patterson AFB). Signed in Paris December 14, 1995. Milosevic represented Bosnian Serb interests. Facts confirmed.

title: Serbia-Montenegro Recognized — UN Sanctions Suspended
note: UN sanctions suspended late 1995 / lifted 1996 post-Dayton. OSCE admission 1996 confirmed. Facts correct.

title: Belgrade Winter Protests — Zajedno Coalition Challenges Milošević
note: Protests began November 18, 1996. Event says '88 days'. Sources say 55 days of daily protests, running November 1996 to February 1997 (~88 calendar days total). The '88 days' figure is an approximation of the full duration; broadly accurate. Milosevic conceded February 1997 confirmed.

title: Milošević Becomes FRY President — Transfers Power as Federal Consolidation
note: Milosevic elected FRY president by federal parliament July 15, 1997 (assumed office July 23). Facts confirmed.

title: Kosovo War Begins — UCK Insurgency and Serbian Security Forces Clash
note: KLA insurgency began early 1998. Racak massacre was January 15, 1999 (event attributes it to 1998 section but notes it correctly as January 1999). Rambouillet talks early 1999 confirmed. Facts broadly correct.

title: NATO Bombing Campaign — 78 Days of Air Strikes Force Serbian Withdrawal from Kosovo
note: NATO campaign March 24 to June 10, 1999 (78 days). Milošević accepted Resolution 1244 June 10. Facts confirmed.

title: Kosovo Under UN Administration — 200,000 Serbs Flee Province
note: ~200,000-280,000 Kosovo Serbs and non-Albanians fled post-June 1999. Event figure of 200,000 is within the documented range. Facts confirmed.

title: Milošević Indicted by ICTY — First Sitting Head of State Charged
note: ICTY indictment issued May 27, 1999. First sitting head of state indicted by international tribunal — confirmed. Facts correct.

title: Bulldozer Revolution — Milošević Ousted After Disputed Election
note: Presidential election September 24, 2000; Kostunica won with ~55% (official FEC said no majority, triggering runoff claim). October 5 uprising confirmed. Facts correct.

title: Milošević Arrested and Transferred to The Hague
note: Arrested April 1, 2001. Transferred to ICTY June 28-29, 2001. Died in Hague cell March 2006 before conclusion of trial. Kostunica's objections confirmed. Facts correct.

title: Economic Stabilization and IMF Program — Post-Milošević Reform Push
note: Djindjic government launched IMF standby agreement, Paris Club debt relief, privatization in 2001. GDP growth returned. Facts confirmed.

title: Serbia-Montenegro State Union Replaces FRY
note: Constitutional Charter adopted February 4, 2003 (event date correct). Belgrade Agreement was signed March 14, 2002. Javier Solana brokered the deal. Facts confirmed.

title: Prime Minister Zoran Djindjić Assassinated
note: Assassinated March 12, 2003 outside Serbian government building. Zemun Clan organized crime perpetrators confirmed. Described as 'only assassination of democratically elected government leader in post-communist Europe' — this characterization is used in sources. Facts confirmed.

title: Operation Sabre — Crackdown on Organized Crime Following Djindjić Murder
note: Operation Sabre launched after Djindjic assassination; mass arrests of organized crime figures confirmed. Facts correct.

title: Koštunica Becomes Serbian Prime Minister — Democratic but Nationalist Governance
note: Kostunica became PM of Serbia in March 2004 heading DSS minority government. Facts confirmed.

title: March Pogroms in Kosovo — Violence Against Serbs Shocks Region
note: March 17-18, 2004 violence. 19 killed (8 Kosovo Serbs, 11 Kosovo Albanians), over 900 injured, 4,000+ displaced, 35 Serbian Orthodox churches/monasteries destroyed. Event says '19 people killed, 900 injured, 4,000 Kosovo Serbs displaced' — confirmed correct.

title: Serbia Applies for EU Stabilization and Association Agreement
note: Serbia engaged the SAA process from 2005. Conditionality on ICTY cooperation and Mladic confirmed. Facts correct.

title: Montenegro Votes for Independence — Serbia Loses Sea Access
note: Referendum May 21, 2006: 55.5% for independence (EU threshold was 55%). Independence declared June 3, 2006. Serbia became landlocked. Facts confirmed.

title: Serbia Adopts New Constitution — Kosovo Referenced as Serbian Territory
note: Referendum October 28-29, 2006. Passed with ~53% yes, turnout ~53-55%. Preamble references Kosovo and Metohija as integral part. Kosovo Albanians boycotted. Facts confirmed.

title: Ahtisaari Plan Proposes Supervised Kosovo Independence — Serbia Rejects
note: Ahtisaari Plan formally presented March 2007 (event says 'February 2007' — the proposal was publicly stated in February but formally submitted to UN SC in March 2007). Minor date imprecision. Russia veto threat confirmed. Facts broadly correct.

title: Kosovo Declares Unilateral Independence — Belgrade Protests Erupt
note: Independence declared February 17, 2008. Belgrade protests and embassy attacks (US, Croatian embassies) on February 17 and February 21. Facts confirmed.

title: Serbia-Russia Strategic Partnership Deepens — Gas and Geopolitics
note: South Stream agreement signed January 25, 2008. NIS deal (Gazprom acquired 51% stake) finalized December 24, 2008. Event says 'January 2008 giving Gazprom NIS majority stake' — the NIS final contract was December 2008, but the initial agreement was January 2008. Minor imprecision on timing of NIS deal closure.

title: EU-Serbia Stabilization and Association Agreement Signed
note: SAA signed April 29, 2008 in Luxembourg (event says 'April 2008'). Confirmed. Ratification conditions on ICTY cooperation confirmed.

title: Radovan Karadžić Arrested in Belgrade — Fugitive Caught After 13 Years
note: Arrested July 21, 2008 in Batajnica, Belgrade, under alias 'Dr. Dragan David Dabic' working as alternative medicine practitioner. Indicted for genocide at Srebrenica and siege of Sarajevo. Convicted to life imprisonment. Facts confirmed.

title: Serbia Applies for EU Membership
note: Formal application submitted December 22, 2009. Candidate status granted March 1, 2012. Accession negotiations opened January 2014. Facts confirmed.

title: ICJ Advisory Opinion on Kosovo Independence — Blow to Serbian Position
note: ICJ advisory opinion issued July 22, 2010. Found Kosovo's declaration did not violate international law. Serbia pushed UN General Assembly dialogue resolution in response. Facts confirmed.

title: Ratko Mladić Arrested in Serbia — Last Major ICTY Fugitive Caught
note: Arrested May 26, 2011 in Lazarevo near Zrenjanin (not 'a village near Zrenjanin' — Lazarevo is the correct village). Convicted and sentenced to life in 2017. Facts confirmed.

title: Serbia Granted EU Candidate Status
note: Candidate status granted March 1, 2012. Accession negotiations opened January 2014. Facts confirmed.

title: SNS Wins Elections — Nikolic and Vucic Rise to Power
note: FALSE: In the 2012 parliamentary elections SNS won ~25% of the popular vote and 73 seats (not a dominant majority). A coalition government was formed led by SPS's Ivica Dacic, not SNS directly. Vucic became First Deputy PM. The description 'won the May 2012 parliamentary elections' with implied dominance is misleading — SNS did not win an outright parliamentary majority in 2012. They formed a coalition under Dacic. The dominant SNS victory came in 2014 (158 seats). The event materially overstates SNS's 2012 parliamentary result.

title: Brussels Agreement — Serbia and Kosovo Sign Normalization Deal
note: Signed April 19, 2013. Mediated by Catherine Ashton. 15-point agreement requiring dissolution of parallel Serb structures in northern Kosovo. Facts confirmed.

title: Catastrophic Floods — Worst Natural Disaster in Serbian Modern History
note: May 2014 floods worst in over 100 years. Event says 'at least 57 people killed in Serbia' — sources report 35-62 deaths across the region; Serbia-specific figure of 57 is on the high end of estimates but plausible. Major displacement confirmed. Facts broadly correct.

title: Vučić Becomes Prime Minister — SNS One-Party Dominance Consolidates
note: April 2014 elections (held March 16, 2014 — event says April). SNS-led coalition won ~48% of votes and 158 seats. Facts confirmed except election date was March 16, not April — minor error.

title: Serbia Joins Chinese Belt and Road Initiative — Infrastructure Investments
note: Belgrade-Budapest railway and E763 motorway (Milos Veliki) confirmed as BRI projects with Chinese financing. Serbia among first European countries to formally align with BRI. Facts confirmed.

title: Vučić Elected President — Executive Power Transfers to Presidency
note: Vucic won April 2, 2017 presidential election with 55.08% in first round. Facts confirmed.

title: Media Pluralism Crisis — Independent Media Under Systematic Pressure
note: EU institutions and Reporters Without Borders documented media deterioration in Serbia in 2018. Serbia's low press freedom rankings confirmed. Facts confirmed.

title: Alliance for Serbia Protests — Sustained Anti-Government Movement
note: Protests under Alliance for Serbia ran from December 2018 through mid-2019 (weekly marches). Peaceful character and six-month duration confirmed. Facts confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic — State of Emergency Declared, Army Deployed
note: State of emergency declared March 15, 2020 (first since 1999 NATO bombing confirmed). Army deployed to hospitals. Elections held June 21, 2020. Facts confirmed.

title: Anti-Government Protests After Election — Crowds Storm Parliament
note: Protests erupted July 7-8, 2020; crowds entered parliament building. Triggered by COVID curfew reimposition after June 2020 elections. Facts confirmed.

title: Lithium Discovery — Jadar Project Stirs Environmental Controversy
note: Permits cancelled January 2022. Project revived July 2024 (confirmed). The event assigns this to 2021, which is when controversy peaked; cancellation was January 2022. Factually the controversy escalated in 2021 with protests. Facts broadly correct.

title: Serbia Refuses to Sanction Russia Over Ukraine Invasion
note: Serbia voted for UN resolutions condemning Russia but refused to join Western sanctions. Energy dependence and Kosovo veto cited. Facts confirmed.

title: SNS Wins April Elections — Opposition Disputes Results
note: April 3, 2022 elections confirmed. Vucic re-elected president. OSCE cited irregularities. Facts confirmed.

title: Banjska Incident — Serbian Armed Group Attacks Kosovo Police
note: September 24, 2023 confirmed. ~80 armed men (not '30' as event states). One Kosovo police officer killed, three attackers killed. Radoicic was SNS vice president who resigned and admitted organizing attack. Event says 'approximately 30 heavily armed men' — sources say approximately 80. Minor factual discrepancy on group size.

title: Ribnikar School Shooting — Serbia's First Mass School Killing
note: May 3, 2023 confirmed. Shooter was 13 years old. 9 students + 1 security guard killed initially (10th victim, a critically injured girl, died May 15). Event says '9 fellow students and one security guard' — confirmed as the initial count (later 10 total). Mladenovac attack two days later killed 8-9 people. Civil society response confirmed. Facts correct.

title: November Station Roof Collapse — 15 Killed at Novi Sad
note: FALSE: The collapse occurred November 1, 2024, not November 1, 2023. The event year is off by one year. The death toll was 14-16 (not 15), ultimately rising to 16 with a later death. Year error = FALSE.

title: December Elections Disputed — 'Serbia Against Violence' Protests Begin
note: December 17, 2023 elections confirmed. Voter busing allegations (40,000+ unregistered Belgrade voters) confirmed by OSCE. Serbia Against Violence coalition protests began December 18. Facts confirmed.

title: Anti-Government Protests Persist — Largest Since 2000
note: 2024-2025 protest movement triggered by Novi Sad station collapse (November 2024) and election disputes. Student-led blockades, university strikes, motorway blockades confirmed. Largest protests since 2000 characterization used in sources. Facts confirmed.

title: EU Reopens Jadar Lithium Project Under Critical Minerals Agreement
note: Constitutional Court ruling restored Rio Tinto's license July 2024. EU-Serbia MoU on critical raw materials signed July 19, 2024. Facts confirmed.
